scope: remaining 29 measure-theory canonical sources after prior batches

reviews.evidence: The definition is norm convergence in an Lp space; sequence, Lp space, measure space, and essential supremum for p=infinity are direct.
The definition quantifies measurable function sequences on a measure space and measures error sets; all listed prerequisites are direct.
The hypotheses require measure space, measurable functions, a.e. convergence, L1 domination, integrability, and integration; the listed mapping matches.
The bound is defined for measurable functions on a measure space outside an a.e. exceptional set; added almost-everywhere.
The core is a function attached to a subset; function and subset are sufficient, while measurability is a later conditional property.
Jordan content is built from finite unions of intervals/rectangles; interval is the direct foundation.
The criterion assumes a bounded function on a closed interval and identifies discontinuities as a Lebesgue null set; listed foundations are direct.
Integrability is finite integral of absolute value for a measurable function on a measure space; all listed prerequisites are direct.
The construction takes measurable nonnegative functions, approximating simple functions and taking a supremum; each listed foundation is used.
The signed integral is defined from positive/negative parts via the nonnegative integral on a measure space; mapping is direct.
The construction starts from outer measure and Caratheodory measurability and produces a measure using measurable rectangles; mapping is direct.
The refinement lemma assumes metric space, compact set, and open cover; the listed topology prerequisites and parent lemma are direct.
The quotient definition requires measure space, Lp norm, and a.e. identification; all three are direct.
A measurable set is a subset in a measurable space; those two concepts are direct.
A measurable space is a set with a sigma-algebra; both are direct.
A measure is a function on a measurable space countably additive over sequences and unions; measurable-space, function, sequence, and union are direct.
A measure space is a measurable space equipped with a measure; both components are direct.
The inequality is stated using Lp norms/spaces and the p=infinity essential-supremum cases; listed prerequisites match.
A null set is a measurable set of measure zero in a measure space; listed prerequisites are direct.
The core is a subadditive set function on the power set, using empty set, subsets, sequences, unions, and functions; listed foundations match.
A premeasure is countably additive on a set algebra when the union remains in it; listed empty-set, set-algebra, function, sequence, and union concepts are direct.
The construction combines two measure spaces on a Cartesian product and uses measurable rectangles/sigma-algebras; listed prerequisites are direct.
The pushforward is defined from a measurable map between measurable spaces and a source measure space; listed prerequisites match.
A set algebra uses power set and closure under complements/unions; listed prerequisites are direct.
The notion is simply a subset of Euclidean space having zero Lebesgue measure; Lebesgue measure is the direct prerequisite.
The core closure axioms use power set, complements, countable unions, and sequences; listed foundations are direct.
A simple function is a finite linear combination of indicators of measurable sets; listed function/set/indicator prerequisites are direct.
Tonelli assumes a product measure and nonnegative measurable function and equates iterated integrals; listed prerequisites are direct.
The definition is a family of L1 functions on a measure space with tail control, and sequences occur in the later sequence formulation; listed prerequisites are direct.
